title: US CPI at 3.7% checks rate cut expectations while RBI drains durable liquidity through OMO sales
changed: Global rate expectations adjusted as US headline CPI climbed to 3.7% YoY, while Fed discount rate records showed regional policy debates that challenged assumptions of near-term monetary easing. In Europe, the IMF upgraded UK growth forecasts, while Bank of Japan board member Koeda pointed to prospective policy tightening ahead of a tripartite PBOC-BOJ-BOK policy meeting.

Crude markets faced immediate supply pressure as Category 2 Hurricane Isaias forced production shut-ins along the US Gulf Coast, keeping Brent crude above $80. With India's August balance of payments recording a $5.2 billion deficit, the RBI intervened structurally by opening a dedicated foreign exchange window for public oil marketing companies to purchase dollars directly. The rupee firmed to ₹95.05/$ as forward premiums touched four-year highs.

Domestically, the RBI shifted from temporary absorption to durable liquidity removal. The central bank conducted a ₹25,000 crore OMO bond sale, enforced an official 90% daily minimum Cash Reserve Ratio maintenance rule, and deployed VRRR auctions at a 5.49% cut-off. Overnight money-market rates responded by lifting from 5.34% call levels to hover near 5.70%, reducing secondary VRRR participation to ₹25,533 crore once permanent cash was extracted.

Sovereign debt supply pressured yields across central and state tenors. State governments cleared ₹31,200 crore in fresh auctions with yields reaching 8.16%, while a ₹20,155 crore surge in State Ways and Means advances pointed to continued borrowing requirements. The central government's bond auction cleared at a yield of 7.3955%, alongside a steepening T-bill curve that established a 76 bps spread between 3-month and 12-month tenors.

For your regulatory and compliance obligations, the RBI tightened treasury operations by restricting the re-booking of cancelled foreign exchange derivative contracts and updating inter-bank risk management rules for Authorized Dealers. Specialized lending institutions SIDBI, NABARD, and EXIM Bank received the Fifth Amendment directions governing capital adequacy calculations, formalizing tighter regulatory buffer baselines.

threads.name: US monetary easing pace
threads.note: US CPI climbing to 3.7% YoY and regional Fed discount rate divisions pushed back the timing of rate cuts. Subsequent inflation prints and US Treasury curve adjustments will confirm whether higher-for-longer yields persist.

threads.name: RBI domestic liquidity drainage
threads.note: A formal 90% minimum CRR requirement combined with ₹25,000 crore in OMO bond sales pushed short-term money market rates to 5.70%. VRRR bid volumes and interbank call spreads will show whether the RBI maintains this cash absorption.

threads.name: State bond supply and long yields
threads.note: State Development Loan yields touched 8.16% on ₹31,200 crore of paper, while short-term overdrafts expanded by ₹20,155 crore. Heavy upcoming SDL calendars will determine if the 10-year sovereign spread continues to widen against central paper.

threads.name: Energy costs and dollar liquidity
threads.note: Category 2 Hurricane Isaias shut-ins keep Brent crude above $80 while India manages a $5.2 billion August BoP deficit. The durability of the ₹95.05/$ exchange rate depends on ongoing use of the RBI special dollar facility for public oil marketers.
